checks: The restriction of π to the orthogonal complement of its kernel is a linear isomorphism. Reparametrizing the image preserves halfspace masses, width-one functionals under the dual map, and difference-body polarity. Fubini supplies the exact probability density, not uniform measure on B except where the actual density is constant. For r<D, the section representative is positive in int B by the interior-preimage argument, bounded on a common compact set, and upper semicontinuous by the upper limit of slice indicators. Brunn–Minkowski gives a convex positive set and concave section root there. Composition with the convex decreasing exponent −(D−r)/(r+1) gives the correct extended inverse-power exponent −1/(r+1); endpoints with zero density are assigned +∞. For r=D the constant density times the closed body indicator has these same required properties.

When r=1, a cover through a common point uses both orientations. At any point outside the open support interval, one closed halfline contains the full support and has mass 1=γ₀. No zero-dimensional density theorem or uniform projected law is required.

For strict exterior contact and r≥2, the affine coordinate change sets the contact at zero with t bounded in [a,b] where a>0. The central projection Jacobian t^(r−1) makes φ a probability density and transfers all homogeneous cap masses exactly. Its support lies in a compact set because t≥a, and reverse Fatou on [a,b] gives upper semicontinuity. Taking an interior point (t₀,x₀) of B, all s in a small open neighborhood of x₀/t₀ admit an open interval of t near t₀ with (t,ts)∈int B, proving the required interior positivity. The radial gauge at (1,s) yields the correct exponent −1/r for the r−1 dimensional centerpoint theorem, including r−1=1.

The t=1 restrictions cover the full affine chart and have margin ℓ_i(1,s), whose sign agrees with the original homogeneous margin tℓ_i(1,s) for t>0. A restriction can be the whole chart or empty when its s-linear part vanishes; a whole-chart restriction has mass one, and empty restrictions do not affect covering. Otherwise a cap containing the centerpoint gives the threshold. For boundary contact, translating outward by a supporting normal preserves the cover; each cap indicator converges off its original ν-null boundary, and a finite maximum passes to the limit.

The initial budget forces interior contact. For v∈∂(B−B), c−v cannot be interior to B because c−int B is open and lies in B−B. Translating by −v changes threshold by −ℓ_i(v). The width-one p≤D bound shows any added mass is at most D times the positive part of ℓ_i(v), even if the translated threshold leaves the scalar support. The cap reaching the exterior threshold must have positive ℓ_i(v), giving the claimed gap divided by D.

The support function of conv{ℓ_i} in the primal space is max_i ℓ_i(v); that of (B−B)° is the gauge of B−B. The difference body contains 0 in its interior, so the boundary inequality extends by positive homogeneity to every primal vector and is equivalent by support comparison to the polar inclusion. The positive scaled polar has interior in the full dual space, so spanning follows.
